notes:
- The cover travels between the card and the title page: Opening a title used to cut from the card to a page that faded in over it. The card now records its poster's rectangle on the press itself - the press, not the click, because the page is already composing by then - and the title page takes that rectangle once, draws one copy of the cover above itself, and springs it from the card's size and place to the hero poster's. The page's own poster is hidden until the copy lands, so the hand-off is between two identical pictures rather than a seam. Closing runs the same spring backwards and the cover goes back to the card it came from, then the page dismisses. It works from the Library grid, list and table, Home's rails and sequel cards, search, the schedule, a studio shelf and profile activity; a deep link or a notification has no press behind it, and those opens keep the page's own entrance. The page no longer scales or rises during a flight, because the copy lands on a measured rectangle and moving the page under it would move the target.
- Show more only appears when it has a whole line to show: Every Settings paragraph that did not fit offered Show more, including the ones whose only hidden line was a short last line: tapping it opened the row by that line, which read as a flicker rather than a reveal. A paragraph now collapses only when at least a whole line stays hidden - measured against the width the row actually gives the text - and otherwise prints in full with no button at all. The button is also the control it claimed to be: a pill with a full 48dp press target and the page's press spring, instead of a bare text line that TalkBack could not tell from a caption.
- The title page's dim finally leaves with the page: The scrim that replaced the platform's dim was drawn outside its own alpha layer - a background placed before a graphicsLayer paints under it rather than in it - so the 60% black never followed the page at all: it sat over the list for the page's whole life and went when the window did, which is the cut it was built to remove, moved to the close. The layer now wraps the ink, so the dim rises with the page on open, and a close that has a cover coming home clears it on the faster spring: the poster arrives on a list the reader can already see, instead of one that brightens after the poster has stopped.
- The flying cover is carried, not resized: The flying cover now lifts a shadow that peaks at the middle of the flight and settles to nothing at both ends, where it is the page's poster or the card's artwork again. A shrinking rectangle reads as a resize; a poster with a shadow under it reads as something being carried across the list and set back down.
- The profile banner can be moved left, centre or right: A banner wider than the card is cropped by definition, and which part survived used to be decided by the transform's centre - the reader's own artwork was the one thing the header never let them position. The layout sheet now offers Left, Center and Right: the crop moves to that side of the picture, on the settle spring rather than in a jump, so the banner slides there instead of flickering. A picture that already fits the width has no crop to move and the control leaves it alone. The choice is stored with the banner's shape, and Reset clears it with everything else.
- The profile banner can drift like a moving still: Drift sweeps the banner slowly sideways while the page sits still, so the whole picture reaches both of its own edges - the only way a cover crop can show the artwork it hides. It is off by default, and the position control dims and stops answering while it runs, because the sweep owns the horizontal position while it is moving. Nothing is composed when the picture has no sideways slack, when the page is off screen, or when the reader has zoomed in and taken the gesture, so an idle profile does not keep redrawing a banner nobody can see.
